chunk_findings.detail: The new guard preserves an existing end only when `sess.how` is non-empty, but a normal `session.ended` event can be processed without `how` (the summary-only `session end --summary` path, and any historical `session.ended` event after the new field was introduced). The handler then sets `ended_at` while leaving `how` empty, contradicting the documented invariant that `how` is `""` only while open. A later bare summary event sees `not sess.how` and re-enters the branch, moving `ended_at` to the later event's timestamp. For example, process `session.ended` at T1 with `{"summary":"first"}` followed by `session.ended` at T2 with `{"summary":"second"}`: after the first event the session is ended at T1, but after the second it is ended at T2, so a summary-only update changes the end time instead of only updating `summary`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/handlers/sessions.py:242-245 (`_h_session_ended`)

chunk_findings.detail: The new optional-field refresh only verifies that the existing hook contains the fields emitted by `_entry_options`; it never verifies that undesired optional fields are absent, and the update line `{**h, "type": "command", "command": wanted, **opts}` merges desired options without deleting stale ones. `hookwriters` requests synchronous hooks for all non-`stop` events and `timeout=30`/no background for `session_end`. If a ddflow `session_end` hook already contains a stale `"background": true` (for example copied from the stop hook or left by an earlier install), the `all(h.get(k) == v for k, v in opts.items())` check can still pass because only the requested `timeout` is compared, so `add_hook` returns “already” and leaves the SessionEnd hook background/async. The harness may then not wait for the SessionEnd hook to write the session-end record, even though the current install requests a synchronous 30-second hook.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/claudehooks.py:add_hook

chunk_findings.detail: `previous_lines` filters sessions to those with `s.prompts or s.notes` before choosing the latest closed session, so it can report an older session as the “previous session” when the actual latest closed session has only a summary. For example, agent A has session `S1` closed at 10:00 with a prompt/note, then session `S2` closed at 11:00 by `close_ended` or `session end --summary done` with no prompts or notes. The comprehension excludes `S2`, `max(closed, key=ended_at)` returns `S1`, and the next session is shown `## Previous session (S1, ended 10:00)` with stale hand-over data even though `S2` was the previous session.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/sessions/_lifecycle.py:245

chunk_findings.detail: `test_previous_session_is_shown_fenced_and_bounded` still requires the hand-over text to contain the HTML-escaped form `<ddflow-record` after a previous prompt containing `<ddflow-record>x...`. The Round-2 fixes listed for this change do not include escaping the previous-session prompt/note, and the prior probe showed the previous-session renderer emits the stored text raw. Running this test therefore reaches line 156 with `text` containing raw `<ddflow-record` and no `<ddflow-record`, raising `AssertionError`; the planted tag is not neutralized.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_session_interrupted.py:156

chunk_findings.detail: After a phantom `session.started`, the refresh is `events, st = log.read_all(), fold(log.read_all(), strict=False)`, so the two snapshots are separate locked operations. A second writer that appends a `session.note` (or a `session.ended`) between those reads leaves `events` without that event while `st` already includes it. `record_inflight` / `close_ended` then dedupe or close from disagreeing inputs: the next Stop treats the note as unseen and appends the same in-flight note again, which is the duplicate this round claims to prevent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/setup/hooks.py:331

chunk_findings.detail: A write during lease grace permanently exempts the session from interrupted close. `lease.live(now, grace_s)` treats the hold as live until `renewed_at + ttl_s + grace_s`, but both lapse sources record only the TTL end (`renewed_at + ttl_s`, or `at + ttl_s`). `find_dead` then requires `_epoch(last) <= max(hits)`. Given ttl end t=100, grace 30, a `session.note` at t=110, and a crash at t=115, at now=200 the agent has no live lease so the session is dead, but hits=[100] and 110 <= 100 is false, so `close_interrupted` never appends `session.ended`. The same note keeps winning on every later SessionStart.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/sessions/_lifecycle.py:_lapses

chunk_findings.detail: The “previous session” is not the latest ended session of this agent. The candidate filter requires `s.prompts or s.notes`, then `max(..., key=ended_at)` runs only on that subset. Given session A ended at 10:00 with a prompt, and session B (same agent) ended at 11:00 via `close_ended` with summary `session ended (logout)` and no prompt or note (`holding nothing` writes nothing), `previous_lines` fences A and labels it the previous session. B is the previous session; its summary is never shown.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/sessions/_lifecycle.py:previous_lines

data.title: ddflow/api/setup/hooks.py:331

chunk_findings.detail: The handler uses `sess.how` as the only sentinel for “this session is already ended.” A `session.ended` event without `how` (e.g. a pre-change record after upgrade, or any bare end path that does not set `how`) sets `ended_at` but leaves `how=""`. A later bare `session.ended` event with only a summary then sees `sess.how == ""`, enters the branch, and overwrites `ended_at` with the later event timestamp. For example, an existing record with `ended_at="2026-01-01T00:00:00Z", how=""` followed by a later summary-only end event at `2026-01-02T00:00:00Z` will have its end time moved to the summary time, even though the session ended earlier. The bare later end should update only the summary, not the recorded end time.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/handlers/sessions.py:243 (`_h_session_ended`)

chunk_findings.detail: The idempotence check only verifies that the keys requested by `_entry_options` are present; it never verifies that unrequested `timeout`/`background` keys are absent. For a call with default options, `_entry_options(0, False)` returns an empty dict, so `all(h.get(k) == v for k, v in opts.items())` is vacuously true. If the existing ddflow hook already has the right command and `type`, but contains a stale option such as `"background": true` on a non-stop hook (or `"timeout": 30` on a stop hook), `add_hook` returns “already in” and leaves that option in place. The later update path also only overlays `opts`, so it cannot delete stale option keys. This can leave a hook running in the background or with a timeout when the current configuration asks for neither.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/claudehooks.py:418-422

chunk_findings.detail: The guard `if how or not s.how:` uses the stored end reason as a proxy for whether the session has already ended. For any prior `session.ended` event that did not carry `how` (e.g. events written before this feature, or any bare end), `s.how` remains empty, so a later bare `session.ended` containing only a summary will overwrite `s.ended` with the summary event's timestamp. For example, given one session with `session.ended` at T1 with no `how` (actual end) followed by `session.ended` at T2 with no `how` but `summary="..."`, `_apply_ended` first sets `ended=T1`, then sets `ended=T2`. This contradicts the stated rule that a bare later end (a summary) keeps how/when it ended and can misreport the end time for legacy or bare-ended sessions.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/session_view.py:_apply_ended

chunk_findings.detail: Given a session `sid` that has a recent prompt recorded (within `DOUBLE_FIRE_S`) and is then closed by a `session.ended` event, a delayed duplicate prompt hook for the same prompt can arrive after the end. `record_prompt` sees `is_started(events, sid)` true and `_is_ended(events, sid)` true, so it appends a `session.started` event with `resumed: True` **before** the `_recorded_recently` double-fire check. `_recorded_recently` then suppresses the prompt as a duplicate and returns. The suppressed duplicate event has still reopened the session: `open_sessions` will list `sid` as open and `_is_ended` will report it as not ended, even though no prompt was actually accepted. This violates the double-fire suppression contract and can make closed/dead-session logic treat the session as live.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/sessions/_record.py:record_prompt

chunk_findings.detail: A later `session.ended` whose `how` is non-empty always overwrites a prior close, including the interrupted case this change just special-cased. Given a session already closed as interrupted (`how="interrupted"`, `ended_at`/`last_active` = last write), a delayed Stop — the intent states Stop is async and the harness does not time-limit it — with `{how: "ended"}` and no `last_active` takes the `if how` branch and sets `how="ended"`, `last_active=""`, and `ended_at` to that late event's `ev.ts`. The session no longer records that it was found dead, and its end time is when the late hook was applied, not when it last wrote.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/handlers/sessions.py:_h_session_ended

chunk_findings.detail: When `lease.expired` has no numeric TTL end in `last_ttl_end` (acquire/renew missing from the retained log, or `at` not an int/float so the update on line 135 is skipped), the lapse is the reaper write time. The comment says that time is only an upper bound, but `find_dead` treats it as the instant the session must have written after. Given a still-open session whose last `session.*` event is at t=150, a real lease end at t=100, and a `lease.expired` at t=500 with no prior numeric TTL for that item, `hits` is [500], `150 <= 500` holds, and the next SessionStart closes that session `interrupted` even though it wrote after the lease actually ended and may still be working without a live hold.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/sessions/_lifecycle.py:142

chunk_findings.detail: `previous_lines` keeps only closed sessions that have prompts, notes, or a summary, then labels `max(ended_at)` as "Previous session". Given S1 ended at T1 with a prompt, S2 ended interrupted at T2 with summary "" and no prompts or notes, and S3 starts, the lines name S1, not S2, so the hand-over attributes an older session's prompt to the wrong predecessor.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/sessions/_lifecycle.py:255

chunk_findings.detail: `_lapse` appends `lease.acquired` with `at=time.time()` and `ttl_s=60`, then `lease.expired` immediately. The TTL end is still ~60s ahead, so the lease has not lapsed. `test_close_interrupted_writes_how_and_the_fold_ends_at_last_active` (comment: "a lease of a1 that already ran out"), `test_close_is_capped_by_the_knob`, and `test_session_start_closes_a_dead_session_and_shows_the_previous_one` all require that fixture to be dead and closed as interrupted. The same file's `test_a_late_expiry_record_does_not_hide_writes_made_after_the_real_lapse` treats lapse as `at+ttl_s`, not the `lease.expired` timestamp. On that rule, `close_interrupted` at the current wall clock must return no sessions; these asserts only pass if an early expiry record is wrongly used as the lapse.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_session_interrupted.py:_lapse

chunk_findings.detail: The dead session is seeded on `EventLog(repo, "a1")`, then `_hook(..., agent="a1")` is expected to close it and echo "last words of the dead". The other hook tests in this file (`test_session_end_hook_closes_the_session_with_its_reason`, `test_stop_with_the_note_off_writes_nothing`) observe the same `_hook` helper on `EventLog(repo, "p")`. Those logs are different files. If hook I/O is "p", session_start never sees the a1 session, the message lacks that text, and folding the a1 log never shows `how == "interrupted"`. If hook I/O is the agent argument, the session_end test folds the wrong log and cannot find the harness session it asserts.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_session_interrupted.py:test_session_start_closes_a_dead_session_and_shows_the_previous_one

chunk_findings.detail: A write during lease grace permanently exempts the session from interrupted close. `lease.live(now, grace_s)` treats the hold as live until `renewed_at + ttl_s + grace_s`, but both lapse sources record only the TTL end (`renewed_at + ttl_s`, or `at + ttl_s`). `find_dead` then requires `_epoch(last) <= max(hits)`. chunk_findings.detail: The handler uses `sess.how` as the only sentinel for “this session is already ended.” A `session.ended` event without `how` (e.g. a pre-change record after upgrade, or any bare end path that does not set `how`) sets `ended_at` but leaves `how=""`. A later bare `session.ended` event with only a summary then sees `sess.how == ""`, enters the branch, and overwrites `ended_at` with the later event timestamp. For example, an existing record with `ended_at="2026-01-01T00:00:00Z", how=""` followed by a later summary-only end event at `2026-01-02T00:00:00Z` will have its end time moved to the summary time, even though the session ended earlier. The bare later end should update only the summary, not the recorded end time.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/handlers/sessions.py:243 (`_h_session_ended`)

chunk_findings.detail: The idempotence check only verifies that the keys requested by `_entry_options` are present; it never verifies that unrequested `timeout`/`background` keys are absent. For a call with default options, `_entry_options(0, False)` returns an empty dict, so `all(h.get(k) == v for k, v in opts.items())` is vacuously true. If the existing ddflow hook already has the right command and `type`, but contains a stale option such as `"background": true` on a non-stop hook (or `"timeout": 30` on a stop hook), `add_hook` returns “already in” and leaves that option in place. The later update path also only overlays `opts`, so it cannot delete stale option keys. This can leave a hook running in the background or with a timeout when the current configuration asks for neither.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/claudehooks.py:418-422

chunk_findings.detail: The guard `if how or not s.how:` uses the stored end reason as a proxy for whether the session has already ended. For any prior `session.ended` event that did not carry `how` (e.g. events written before this feature, or any bare end), `s.how` remains empty, so a later bare `session.ended` containing only a summary will overwrite `s.ended` with the summary event's timestamp. For example, given one session with `session.ended` at T1 with no `how` (actual end) followed by `session.ended` at T2 with no `how` but `summary="..."`, `_apply_ended` first sets `ended=T1`, then sets `ended=T2`. This contradicts the stated rule that a bare later end (a summary) keeps how/when it ended and can misreport the end time for legacy or bare-ended sessions.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/session_view.py:_apply_ended

chunk_findings.detail: Given a session `sid` that has a recent prompt recorded (within `DOUBLE_FIRE_S`) and is then closed by a `session.ended` event, a delayed duplicate prompt hook for the same prompt can arrive after the end. `record_prompt` sees `is_started(events, sid)` true and `_is_ended(events, sid)` true, so it appends a `session.started` event with `resumed: True` **before** the `_recorded_recently` double-fire check. `_recorded_recently` then suppresses the prompt as a duplicate and returns. The suppressed duplicate event has still reopened the session: `open_sessions` will list `sid` as open and `_is_ended` will report it as not ended, even though no prompt was actually accepted. This violates the double-fire suppression contract and can make closed/dead-session logic treat the session as live.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/sessions/_record.py:record_prompt

chunk_findings.detail: A later `session.ended` whose `how` is non-empty always overwrites a prior close, including the interrupted case this change just special-cased. Given a session already closed as interrupted (`how="interrupted"`, `ended_at`/`last_active` = last write), a delayed Stop — the intent states Stop is async and the harness does not time-limit it — with `{how: "ended"}` and no `last_active` takes the `if how` branch and sets `how="ended"`, `last_active=""`, and `ended_at` to that late event's `ev.ts`. The session no longer records that it was found dead, and its end time is when the late hook was applied, not when it last wrote.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/handlers/sessions.py:_h_session_ended

chunk_findings.detail: When `lease.expired` has no numeric TTL end in `last_ttl_end` (acquire/renew missing from the retained log, or `at` not an int/float so the update on line 135 is skipped), the lapse is the reaper write time. The comment says that time is only an upper bound, but `find_dead` treats it as the instant the session must have written after. Given a still-open session whose last `session.*` event is at t=150, a real lease end at t=100, and a `lease.expired` at t=500 with no prior numeric TTL for that item, `hits` is [500], `150 <= 500` holds, and the next SessionStart closes that session `interrupted` even though it wrote after the lease actually ended and may still be working without a live hold.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/sessions/_lifecycle.py:142

chunk_findings.detail: `previous_lines` keeps only closed sessions that have prompts, notes, or a summary, then labels `max(ended_at)` as "Previous session". Given S1 ended at T1 with a prompt, S2 ended interrupted at T2 with summary "" and no prompts or notes, and S3 starts, the lines name S1, not S2, so the hand-over attributes an older session's prompt to the wrong predecessor.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/sessions/_lifecycle.py:255

chunk_findings.detail: `_lapse` appends `lease.acquired` with `at=time.time()` and `ttl_s=60`, then `lease.expired` immediately. The TTL end is still ~60s ahead, so the lease has not lapsed. `test_close_interrupted_writes_how_and_the_fold_ends_at_last_active` (comment: "a lease of a1 that already ran out"), `test_close_is_capped_by_the_knob`, and `test_session_start_closes_a_dead_session_and_shows_the_previous_one` all require that fixture to be dead and closed as interrupted. The same file's `test_a_late_expiry_record_does_not_hide_writes_made_after_the_real_lapse` treats lapse as `at+ttl_s`, not the `lease.expired` timestamp. On that rule, `close_interrupted` at the current wall clock must return no sessions; these asserts only pass if an early expiry record is wrongly used as the lapse.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_session_interrupted.py:_lapse

chunk_findings.detail: The dead session is seeded on `EventLog(repo, "a1")`, then `_hook(..., agent="a1")` is expected to close it and echo "last words of the dead". The other hook tests in this file (`test_session_end_hook_closes_the_session_with_its_reason`, `test_stop_with_the_note_off_writes_nothing`) observe the same `_hook` helper on `EventLog(repo, "p")`. Those logs are different files. If hook I/O is "p", session_start never sees the a1 session, the message lacks that text, and folding the a1 log never shows `how == "interrupted"`. If hook I/O is the agent argument, the session_end test folds the wrong log and cannot find the harness session it asserts.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_session_interrupted.py:test_session_start_closes_a_dead_session_and_shows_the_previous_one

chunk_findings.detail: The new guard preserves an existing end only when `sess.how` is non-empty, but a normal `session.ended` event can be processed without `how` (the summary-only `session end --summary` path, and any historical `session.ended` event after the new field was introduced). The handler then sets `ended_at` while leaving `how` empty, contradicting the documented invariant that `how` is `""` only while open. A later bare summary event sees `not sess.how` and re-enters the branch, moving `ended_at` to the later event's timestamp. For example, process `session.ended` at T1 with `{"summary":"first"}` followed by `session.ended` at T2 with `{"summary":"second"}`: after the first event the session is ended at T1, but after the second it is ended at T2, so a summary-only update changes the end time instead of only updating `summary`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/handlers/sessions.py:242-245 (`_h_session_ended`)

chunk_findings.detail: The new optional-field refresh only verifies that the existing hook contains the fields emitted by `_entry_options`; it never verifies that undesired optional fields are absent, and the update line `{**h, "type": "command", "command": wanted, **opts}` merges desired options without deleting stale ones. `hookwriters` requests synchronous hooks for all non-`stop` events and `timeout=30`/no background for `session_end`. If a ddflow `session_end` hook already contains a stale `"background": true` (for example copied from the stop hook or left by an earlier install), the `all(h.get(k) == v for k, v in opts.items())` check can still pass because only the requested `timeout` is compared, so `add_hook` returns “already” and leaves the SessionEnd hook background/async. The harness may then not wait for the SessionEnd hook to write the session-end record, even though the current install requests a synchronous 30-second hook.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/claudehooks.py:add_hook

chunk_findings.detail: `previous_lines` filters sessions to those with `s.prompts or s.notes` before choosing the latest closed session, so it can report an older session as the “previous session” when the actual latest closed session has only a summary. For example, agent A has session `S1` closed at 10:00 with a prompt/note, then session `S2` closed at 11:00 by `close_ended` or `session end --summary done` with no prompts or notes. The comprehension excludes `S2`, `max(closed, key=ended_at)` returns `S1`, and the next session is shown `## Previous session (S1, ended 10:00)` with stale hand-over data even though `S2` was the previous session.
